brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Property tax relief program for seniors and persons retired due to physical disability; mentions retirement status and pension income only as factors in determining eligibility and income thresholds for property tax exemptions, not as a pension system measure.

brief: Providing tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Provides property tax exemptions for seniors and disabled persons based on income, but does not affect pension systems or benefits.

brief: Creating the license suspension review committee.
triage_how: Creates a license suspension review committee to hear appeals from commercial fishers facing suspension or revocation of fishing privileges for regulatory violations.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired due to physical disability.
triage_how: Property tax exemption and deferral relief for seniors and persons retired due to physical disability, based on income and age criteria, with no substantive effect on public retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Creating a housing allowance program for nonsupervisory educational employees.
haiku_summary: The bill creates a housing allowance program for nonsupervisory K-12 employees and excludes these allowances from earnable compensation used to calculate public retirement system benefits.

brief: Increasing the monthly pensions for volunteer fire fighters and reserve officers.
triage_how: The bill amends RCW sections governing LEOFF to increase monthly pensions for volunteer firefighters and reserve officers: raising the standard pension from $280 to $300 monthly for 25-plus years of service and the minimum pension from $30 to $50 monthly.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Bill provides property tax exemptions for senior citizens and persons no longer working due to physical disability based on income thresholds.

brief: Providing for reimbursement of public entities for payments made because of criminal acts of officers, employees, or contractors.
haiku_summary: The bill permits courts to order assignment of retirement benefits to public entities as reimbursement for damages caused by members' felonious criminal conduct, creating an exception to the standard exemption of retirement benefits from execution and attachment.

brief: Providing annual increases in retirement allowances.
haiku_summary: The bill extends the deadline from July 1 to December 31 of the calendar year for retirees to attain age 66 in order to qualify for annual retirement allowance increases under PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1.

brief: Determining which fire fighters or law enforcement officers may elect or be elected to certain pension and disability boards.
haiku_summary: The bill limits voting in pension and disability board elections to active and retired fire fighters and law enforcement officers subject to board jurisdiction, while expanding eligibility to serve on boards to all active and retired members employed by or retired from the municipality or county.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system plan 1 to use extended school years for calculation of their earnable compensation.
haiku_summary: The bill authorizes TRS Plan 1 members teaching in extended school year programs to calculate earnable compensation using extended school years instead of fiscal years.

brief: Correcting retirement system statutes.
haiku_summary: The bill makes technical corrections to retirement system statutes, expands service credit portability eligibility from LEOFF to additional plans, and clarifies benefit accrual provisions across multiple retirement systems.

brief: Allowing a member holding state elective office the option during each term of office of membership or retirement and beginning their retirement allowance in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, the teachers' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the public employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill grants members holding state elective office the option at the beginning of each term to end membership and commence their retirement allowance, or to resume membership in their retirement system.

brief: Allowing fire fighter emergency medical technicians to transfer public employees' retirement system service credit to the law enforcement of
triage_how: The bill allows fire fighter emergency medical technicians who previously accrued service credit in the Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) to elect an irrevocable transfer of that service credit to the Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System (LEOFF) Plan 2, subject to a five-year waiting period and additional contributions to cover the difference in plan provisions.

brief: Providing optional service credit for substitute service to members of the school employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill enables substitute school employees to optionally purchase service credit for substitute service work performed, counting that prior service toward their retirement benefits under SERS.

brief: Creating the select committee on pension policy.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes a select committee on pension policy to oversee pension issues across state retirement systems, replacing the previous joint committee structure, and creates a state actuary appointment committee with representation from legislators, active members, retirees, and employers.

brief: Addressing the department of fish and wildlife law enforcement officers' membership in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 for periods of future service.
haiku_summary: The bill adds Department of Fish and Wildlife law enforcement officers to Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System Plan 2 membership, moving PERS Plans 2 and 3 members to LEOFF Plan 2 while PERS Plan 1 members remain in PERS.

brief: Making optional plan 3 member contributions.
haiku_summary: The bill modifies Plan 3 member contribution rates in three retirement systems, establishing a mandatory 5 percent base plus optional discretionary rates up to 10 percent, and permits annual rate changes.

brief: Paying survivor benefits in accordance with Title 26 U.S.C. Sec. 101(h) as amended by the Fallen Hero Survivor Benefit Fairness Act of 2001.
triage_how: Bill adds a new section to RCW 41.04 requiring that retirement survivor benefits paid to beneficiaries of public safety officers who die in the line of duty comply with federal tax code 26 U.S.C. Sec. 101(h).

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the public employees' retirement system to
triage_how: Allows members of TRS, SERS, and PERS to receive retirement benefits beginning at age seventy and one-half while remaining employed without reduction in pension.

brief: Retiring early in the public employees' retirement system, plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill consolidates PERS Plan 2 early retirement options by establishing a fixed 3 percent annual reduction to the retirement allowance and eliminating a separate alternate early retirement provision.

brief: Vesting after five years of service in the defined benefit portion of the public employees' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the teachers' retirement system plan 3.
haiku_summary: The bill reduces the vesting requirement from ten to five service credit years for normal retirement eligibility at age 65 or older in the defined benefit portions of PERS, SERS, and TRS Plan 3.

brief: Limiting the rule-making authority of certain entities to those instances where there is a specific grant of legislative authority.
haiku_summary: Requires the Department of Retirement Systems director to adopt rules only from specific legislative grants of authority rather than general enabling provisions.

brief: Establishing the retirement age for members of the Washington state patrol retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill raises the mandatory retirement age for Washington State Patrol members from 60 to 65 years, effective July 1, 2003.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens or persons retired due to physical disability.
triage_how: Provides property tax exemptions to seniors and persons no longer employed due to physical disability; does not substantively concern public retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Making 2003-05 operating appropriations.
haiku_summary: Authorizes the legislature to transfer excess administrative expense fund balance from the Department of Retirement Systems to the state general fund during the 2003-2005 fiscal biennium.

brief: Providing health care coverage for retired or disabled school employees and retired state employees.
triage_how: The bill extends health insurance coverage eligibility to retired or disabled employees receiving retirement allowances from Washington public pension systems (TRS and PERS).

brief: Making an additional payment to certain plan 1 and plan 3 retirees.
triage_how: Distributes extraordinary investment gains to Plan 1 and Plan 3 retirees as additional lump sum payments and member account credits, with Plan 1 receiving odd-year payments beginning 2005 and Plan 3 receiving account credits on even years beginning 2004.

brief: Consolidating state functions that are necessary to implement the 2003-2005 omnibus operating appropriations bill.
haiku_summary: Consolidates the Department of Retirement Systems into the Department of Human Resources, transferring administrative oversight and governance structure without changing retirement benefit formulas, contribution rates, or member eligibility rules.

brief: Making human services-related statutory changes necessary to implement the 2003-2005 omnibus operating appropriations bill.
triage_how: The bill makes only human services-related statutory changes to implement the 2003-2005 omnibus operating appropriations bill and does not substantively affect public retirement benefits or systems.

brief: Making general government-related statutory changes necessary to implement the 2003-2005 omnibus operating appropriations bill.
haiku_summary: The bill adjusts employer and member contribution rates for public retirement systems and updates long-term economic assumptions in actuarial valuations to reflect improved funding status, with an effective date of July 1, 2003.

brief: Authorizing retirement incentive programs.
haiku_summary: The bill authorizes public employers to temporarily offer early retirement incentives to employees facing workforce reduction, facility closure, or privatization, with employers required to cover full actuarial system costs.

brief: Changing provisions relating to the summary suspension of a liquor license pending revocation proceedings.
triage_how: Bill regulates liquor license suspension and revocation procedures through the Liquor Control Board, with no connection to pension or retirement benefit systems.

brief: Reorganizing criminal statutes within the RCW.
haiku_summary: The bill reorganizes the statement of criminal penalties for retirement system fraud, changing references from general felony language to specific class B felony designations conforming to revised criminal code structure, without affecting substantive retirement system provisions.

brief: Authorizing early retirement for public employees' retirement system plan 1 and plan 2 members.
triage_how: Creates a temporary early retirement option for PERS Plan 1 and Plan 2 members (2003), granting service credit bonuses of one additional year per five years of actual service (max 30 years total) for members retiring by September 30, 2003.

brief: Addressing the parks and recreation commission law enforcement officers' membership in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 for periods of future service.
haiku_summary: The bill makes state parks and recreation commission law enforcement officers who were in Public Employees' Retirement System Plan 2 or 3 members of the Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System Plan 2, while Plan 1 members remain in PERS.

brief: Participating in insurance plans and contracts by separated plan 2 members of certain retirement systems.
triage_how: Extends state health insurance eligibility to separated Plan 2 members of public retirement systems who are age 55 with 10+ years of service.

brief: Concerning park rangers employed by the parks and recreation commission.
haiku_summary: The bill designates state park rangers as law enforcement peace officers but explicitly excludes them from membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System.

brief: Calculating the death benefits for members of the teachers' retirement system, school employees' retirement system, and public employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill removes actuarial reductions from survivor retirement benefits for members of public retirement systems who are killed in the course of employment, requiring payment of unreduced retirement allowances to beneficiaries.

brief: Concerning the postretirement employment of retirees by school districts.
triage_how: Restricts school districts from hiring public pension retirees for postretirement employment for more than two consecutive school years without superintendent approval based on local labor market availability.

brief: Concerning unemployment benefits paid to retirees.
triage_how: The bill excludes post-retirement employment wages from unemployment insurance base-year calculations for retirees of Washington's public pension systems by anchoring definitions of employer and retiree to PERS, TRS, SERS, and LEOFF statutes.

brief: Providing service credit for military service during the Vietnam conflict.
haiku_summary: The bill allows public employees' retirement system members who are Vietnam conflict veterans to receive up to five years of military service credit toward retirement benefits after completing twenty-five years of creditable service.

brief: Changing provisions relating to the administrative office of the courts.
haiku_summary: Standardizes terminology throughout RCW sections by replacing references to "administrator for the courts" with "administrative office of the courts," including in provisions governing disposition of judicial retirement account death benefits.

brief: Governing the Washington state patrol retirement system, plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes an independent board of trustees for the Washington State Patrol retirement system plan 1 with exclusive fiduciary authority to adopt actuarial standards, design enhanced benefits within contribution limits, and manage system assets independently from the statewide pension funding council.

brief: Concerning industrial insurance medical examinations.
triage_how: The bill establishes procedures for medical examinations under workers' compensation, a benefit system categorically distinct from public pension systems, with no effects on retirement eligibility, accrual, contributions, or benefit calculations.

brief: Allowing public safety workers to retire early in the public employees' retirement system, plan 2.
haiku_summary: Creates an alternative early retirement option under PERS Plan 2 for public safety workers who have completed 20 years of service credit and reached age 55, with retirement benefits reduced by 3 percent per year until age 65.

brief: Addressing the liquor control board law enforcement officers' membership in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 for periods of future service.
haiku_summary: Transfers liquor control board law enforcement officers from the Public Employees' Retirement System to the Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System Plan 2, establishing dual membership without transfer of service credit.

brief: Modifying industrial insurance wage provisions.
triage_how: Bill modifies workers' compensation wage definitions and benefit calculations under Title 51, excluding pension contributions from compensable wages but not affecting public retirement systems.

brief: Enhancing industrial insurance vocational rehabilitation benefits.
triage_how: This bill amends workers' compensation vocational rehabilitation benefits under the industrial insurance program, which is separate from public retirement pension systems.

brief: Adopting standards under industrial insurance for rating pain-related impairments.
triage_how: Establishes rating standards for work-related impairments under industrial insurance (workers' compensation), not public employee pension systems.

brief: Securing hearing loss benefits.
triage_how: Establishes timing rules for noise-induced hearing loss workers' compensation claims and standards for hearing aid provision and upgrading.

brief: Protecting persons with a history of timely child support payments from mandatory wage assignment orders.
triage_how: Bill modifies child support wage assignment procedures; does not interact with or affect public retirement systems.

brief: Authorizing advanced registered nurse practitioners to examine, diagnose, and treat injured workers covered by industrial insurance.
triage_how: Expands nurse practitioner scope of practice in workers' compensation; does not affect retirement benefits or systems.

brief: Increasing public employees' retirement system, plan 1 members' monetary compensation for accrued sick leave.
triage_how: Increases sick-leave buyout compensation at retirement for PERS Plan 1 members from a one-to-four ratio to a one-to-two ratio of accrued sick leave.

brief: Extending death benefits to certain surviving spouses under the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill expands death benefits eligibility under LEOFF to include surviving spouses married for at least five years who are at least age fifty-five, providing an exception to the one-year marriage requirement.

brief: Revising provisions relating to inmate funds.
triage_how: Amends workers' compensation benefit protections under Title 51 RCW to account for inmate funds in correctional institutions, with no substantive effect on public retirement benefit systems.

brief: Creating the Washington voluntary accounts program.
haiku_summary: The bill creates a voluntary retirement savings program for private sector workers lacking access to employer retirement plans, administered through the Department of Retirement Systems and State Investment Board.

brief: Hiring retired members of the public employees' retirement system plan 1 and the teachers' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill allows retired PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 members to continue receiving pension payments while working up to 1,500 hours annually (with employer approval), raising the threshold at which pension benefits suspend.

brief: Simplifying and adding certainty to the calculation of workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: The bill simplifies workers' compensation benefit calculations by redefining how wages are calculated for benefit purposes, excluding fringe benefits including retirement plans from wage calculations.

brief: Regulating postretirement employment in the public employees' retirement system and the teachers' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill reduces retirement benefits for retirees who return to employment, lowering the annual hour threshold from 1,500 to 867 hours and establishing proportional benefit reductions based on postretirement work hours.

brief: Simplifying and adding certainty to the calculation of workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: Bill addresses only workers compensation benefits and calculations, which is a separate system from public employee retirement pensions.

brief: Managing the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, plan 1.
triage_how: The bill establishes an independent board of trustees to govern the LEOFF Plan 1 retirement system, with member representation and authority to adopt actuarial standards, approve increased benefits subject to contribution limits, and oversee pension administration.

brief: Permitting a retired judge acting as a judge pro tempore to decline compensation.
triage_how: The bill permits retired judges to decline compensation when acting as judges pro tempore, but does not address retirement benefits or public retirement systems.

brief: Changing provisions for school employees' tax deferred annuities.
triage_how: Authorizes school employers and the Washington State Teachers' Retirement System to offer tax-deferred annuity contracts under federal tax code section 403(b) and removes restrictions on employee choice of providers.

brief: Concerning industrial insurance benefits for the surviving beneficiaries of workers whose deaths occurred before 1988.
triage_how: Adjusts death benefits under the industrial insurance (workers' compensation) system for survivors of workers with deaths between 1971 and 1988, applying newer benefit formulas to cases meeting specific eligibility criteria.

brief: Authorizing collection of support payments for children with developmental disabilities in out-of-home care.
triage_how: Bill amends child welfare statutes to strengthen child support collection from parents of children with developmental disabilities in out-of-home care; has no effect on retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Authorizing early retirement.
haiku_summary: Establishes a temporary early retirement option from September 2003 through February 2004 for public employees and teachers ages 60 and older with at least five years of service to retire with benefits reduced 3 percent annually for each year before age 65.

brief: Making an irrevocable choice to waive rights to the defined benefit under the plan 3 retirement systems.
triage_how: Bill allows public employee pension members to irrevocably waive defined benefit rights after receiving a distribution.

brief: Implementing Initiative Measure No. 790.
haiku_summary: Establishes independent board governance structure for the law enforcement officers' and firefighters' retirement system plan 2 with authority to adopt contribution rates biennially.

brief: Implementing Initiative Measure No. 790.
haiku_summary: The bill transfers authority for setting LEOFF plan 2 contribution rates from the state contribution rate council to a newly created independent LEOFF plan 2 retirement board, establishing separate governance and funding mechanisms for that plan.

brief: Removing the allocation of excess earnings from section 6 of Initiative Measure No. 790.
haiku_summary: The bill eliminates automatic allocation of excess investment earnings above the actuarially assumed rate of return to provide additional benefits for LEOFF members.

brief: Funding the state retirement systems.
haiku_summary: The bill modifies actuarial funding methodology by extending asset value smoothing from a fixed four-year to a variable up-to-eight-year period and suspends unfunded liability payments for public employees' and teachers' retirement systems, resulting in adjusted employer and member contribution rates for four state retirement systems effective July 2003.

brief: Concerning services for persons with developmental disabilities.
triage_how: The bill amends services and eligibility for persons with developmental disabilities under Title 71A RCW and does not affect public retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Concerning hearing loss claims.
triage_how: Bill addresses workers' compensation hearing loss claims and benefits; does not affect public retirement systems.

brief: Concerning workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: The bill amends workers' compensation benefit calculations but does not substantively affect public retirement systems; the only retirement reference excludes retirement plans from wage definitions for compensation purposes.

brief: Concerning workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: Bill amends workers' compensation benefit calculations for injury cases; references to 'pension' in the text denote workers' compensation disability pensions, not public employee retirement pensions.

brief: Limiting the rule-making authority of certain entities to those instances where there is a specific grant of legislative authority.
haiku_summary: The bill restricts the Department of Retirement Systems director's authority to adopt administrative rules only when there is a specific statutory grant of legislative authority, effective July 1, 2004.

brief: Collecting reimbursement from certain public officers and employees.
haiku_summary: Court-ordered reimbursement of paid investigative leave compensation for convicted public officers and employees may be collected from their public retirement benefits despite statutory benefit exemptions.

brief: Raising the sixty percent cap on retirement allowances from the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: Raises the maximum retirement allowance for LEOFF Plan 1 members from sixty to seventy percent of final average salary.

brief: Providing benefits to certain disabled members of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: Creates a minimum disability retirement allowance for LEOFF Plan 2 members disabled in the line of duty, equal to 10 percent of final average salary plus 2 percent per year of service beyond 5.

brief: Calculating the retirement allowance of a member of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 who is killed in the course of employment.
haiku_summary: The bill removes the actuarial reduction applied to the retirement allowance paid to survivors when a Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System member is killed in the course of employment.

brief: Excluding certain veteran benefits from the income calculation for the retired person property tax relief program.
triage_how: Excludes military disability benefits from income calculations for the retired person property tax relief program, not modifying pension systems.

brief: Increasing the combined disposable income eligibility threshold for the retired persons property tax relief program.
triage_how: Increases combined disposable income thresholds for a property tax relief program serving aged and disabled retired persons, independent of public pension systems.

brief: Allowing suspension of fines involving parking by disabled persons.
triage_how: The bill modifies disabled parking permit rules to allow courts to suspend fines for violations only upon finding exceptional circumstances, unrelated to public retirement systems or pension benefits.

brief: Adding license suspension for driving under the influence for purposes of vehicular homicide.
triage_how: The bill amends vehicular homicide statutes to enhance penalties for driving with a suspended license and does not address public retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Providing death benefits for members of the Washington state patrol retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill eliminates the actuarial reduction on death benefits for Washington State Patrol Retirement System Plan 2 members killed in the course of employment.

brief: Permitting members of the public employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 and the school employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan
triage_how: Amends PERS and SERS Plans 2 and 3 to permit early-retirement-eligible members to purchase up to five years of additional service credit at actuarial equivalent value.

brief: Permitting members of the public employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 and the school employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 to buy down the early retirement reduction amounts.
haiku_summary: Permits members of PERS and SERS Plans 2 and 3 to pay a lump sum or rollover to reduce or eliminate the actuarial reduction applied to their early retirement benefits.

brief: Establishing a public safety employees' retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes a new public safety employees' retirement system plan 2 for corrections, parks, patrol, and liquor control employees, creating opt-in membership for existing PERS Plan 2/3 members while auto-enrolling new hires.

brief: Establishing a one thousand dollar minimum monthly benefit for public employees' retirement system plan 1 members and teachers' retirement system plan 1 members who have at least twenty five years of service and who have been retired at least twenty years.
haiku_summary: Establishes a $1,000 monthly minimum benefit for PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 members with at least 25 years of service who have been retired at least 20 years, effective July 1, 2004.

brief: Providing annual increases in retirement allowances.
haiku_summary: Extends the deadline for reaching age 66 to December 31 to qualify for annual increases in retirement allowances for PERS and TRS Plan 1 beneficiaries.

brief: Vesting after five years of service in the defined benefit portion of the public employees' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the teachers' retirement system plan 3.
haiku_summary: Shortens the vesting requirement for normal retirement in Plan 3 from ten to five service credit years across PERS, SERS, and TRS.

brief: Establishing an asset smoothing corridor for actuarial valuations used in the funding of the state retirement systems.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes a corridor constraint on asset smoothing methods used in actuarial pension valuations, requiring that the actuarial value of assets not deviate more than 30 percent above or below the market value of plan assets on the valuation date.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system plan 1 who are employed less than full time as psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, or speech language pathologists or audiologists to annualize their salaries when calculating their average final compensation.
haiku_summary: The bill extends salary annualization privileges in retirement benefit calculations to part-time Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members employed as psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech language pathologists, and audiologists.

brief: Authorizing collection of support payments for children with developmental disabilities in out-of-home care.
triage_how: The bill expands child support collection authority for children with developmental disabilities in out-of-home care but does not amend pension law or affect retirement benefit structures.

brief: Regulating the state investment board.
haiku_summary: The bill expands State Investment Board membership from 15 to 18, increases retirement system member representation, creates an audit and accountability committee, and strengthens conflict-of-interest rules and financial reporting requirements.

brief: Restricting teachers' retirement system plan 1 postretirement employment.
haiku_summary: House Bill 2640 reduces the annual postretirement employment threshold for plan 1 teachers from 1,500 to 867 hours, after which pension payments cease, while establishing a limited exception allowing school districts to hire retirees for up to 1,500 hours if procedural requirements including documented justifiable need and school board approval are satisfied.

brief: Providing tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Increases income thresholds and property valuation limits for property tax exemptions for seniors and disabled retirees; updates disposable income calculation to include pension receipts, requiring biennial inflation adjustments thereafter.

brief: Establishing priority for funds in the liability insurance program for retired primary care providers volunteering to serve low-income patie
triage_how: The bill provides liability insurance for retired private-sector healthcare providers volunteering at low-income clinics, with no substantive connection to Washington public employee pension systems or benefits.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Property tax exemption for seniors and persons unable to work due to disability; uses retirement status as eligibility criterion but does not modify pension systems.

brief: Crediting DUI offenders with time already suspended.
triage_how: Bill addresses DUI criminal penalties and driver's license suspension procedures; references to suspension pertain exclusively to license suspension, not pension benefits or retirement systems.

brief: Permitting retired participants to resume volunteer fire fighter, emergency worker, or reserve officer service.
triage_how: The bill permits retired pension recipients to resume volunteer service while remaining in receipt of pensions, subject to medical examinations and modified benefit eligibility.

brief: Removing the sixty percent cap on retirement allowances from the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill eliminates the sixty percent cap on retirement allowances for Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System Plan 1 members, allowing higher pension benefits upon retirement.

brief: Simplifying and adding certainty to the calculation of workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: This bill amends workers' compensation benefit calculation provisions in RCW Title 51 and does not substantively affect public employee retirement systems.

brief: Improving the competitiveness of Washington's industrial insurance system.
triage_how: The bill reforms the industrial insurance (workers' compensation) system through amendments to Title 51 RCW without substantively affecting public retirement pension systems, benefit structures, or calculations.

brief: Expanding the role of self-insurers in the workers' compensation system.
triage_how: The bill addresses workers' compensation self-insurers and claim administration within the RCW 51 system, not public employee pension benefits or systems.

brief: Permitting leave sharing policies for local government employers.
haiku_summary: The bill permits leave sharing compensation to be counted as compensation earnable for retirement benefit calculation purposes in both Teachers' Retirement System and Public Employees' Retirement System.

brief: Providing for individual health insurance for retired and disabled public employees.
triage_how: Bill requires local governments to allow retired and disabled public employees to continue participating in employer health plans, with eligibility defined by pension system retirement or disability status.

brief: Conforming the social security offset provisions of Title 51 RCW to the modified federal social security retirement age and continuing to allow the state to implement an offset otherwise imposed by the federal government.
triage_how: Bill updates workers' compensation social security offset formulas in Title 51 RCW to conform to federal changes in Social Security retirement age, but operates only on workers' compensation—a distinct statutory scheme from public employee pensions.

brief: Regarding industrial insurance benefits induced by fraud.
triage_how: Bill amends workers' compensation (Title 51) fraud procedures and enforcement, not public retirement systems.

brief: Regarding liability for industrial insurance premiums.
triage_how: The bill modifies contractor and corporate officer liability for workers' compensation insurance premiums, not pension or retirement benefits.

brief: Establishing the composition and jurisdiction of city and county disability boards.
haiku_summary: The bill clarifies the composition and territorial jurisdiction of LEOFF disability boards, redefining county board scope from all county residents to employees and retirees of county and other local employers.

brief: Choosing a reduced retirement allowance under the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill extends the deadline for the Department of Retirement Systems to adopt rules allowing LEOFF Plan 1 members to elect an actuarially reduced retirement allowance in exchange for continuing a portion of that benefit to a surviving spouse ineligible for survivor benefits under standard provisions, and allows retirees whose designated spouse predeceases them to receive an increase in their benefit.

brief: Creating a medical account for the catastrophic illnesses of law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 1 members a
triage_how: Establishes a catastrophic medical expense account for LEOFF Plan 1 members and beneficiaries, funded by 6 percent member and employer contributions.

brief: Concerning liability to the department of labor and industries for premiums, overpayments, and penalties.
triage_how: Not applicable; bill concerns worker's compensation insurance, not public retirement systems.

brief: Restricting use of adjustable suspensions.
triage_how: Bill restricts operation of motor vehicles with adjustable suspension systems; entirely unrelated to public employee retirement systems.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired due to physical disability.
triage_how: Provides property tax exemptions and deferrals for seniors and persons retired due to physical disability, using age and income-based eligibility criteria.

brief: Providing property tax relief for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.
triage_how: Bill provides property tax relief for seniors and disabled persons, referencing retirement status and including pension income in disposable income calculations, but does not modify Washington public pension systems or benefits.

brief: Revising the application of social security disability dependency benefits to child support obligations.
triage_how: It addresses federal Social Security disability, retirement, and survivors benefits in the context of child support law, not Washington State public employee pension systems.

brief: Implementing tax reform.
haiku_summary: Bill subjects pension and retirement benefit payments from public systems to the new state income tax (Title 82A RCW) and requires tax withholding by the Department of Retirement Systems.

brief: Implementing tax reform.
haiku_summary: The bill makes retirement and pension benefits from multiple state retirement systems subject to taxation under a new income tax (Title 82A RCW) by amending each system's statute to remove the tax exemption previously applied to such benefits.

brief: Allowing fire fighter emergency medical technicians to transfer public employees' retirement system service credit to the law enforcement of
triage_how: The bill allows emergency medical technicians transitioning from other government departments to fire departments to transfer their accumulated public employees' retirement system service credit to the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2, subject to eligibility and payment conditions.

brief: Determining which fire fighters or law enforcement officers may elect or be elected to certain pension and disability boards.
haiku_summary: The bill restricts voting rights for pension and disability board elections to fire fighters and law enforcement officers subject to the board's jurisdiction, while broadening eligibility to be elected to include all such personnel employed or retired from the relevant city or county.

brief: Making optional plan 3 member contributions.
haiku_summary: Makes Plan 3 member contribution rate choices revisable annually instead of irrevocable, and adds optional contribution rate options above a mandatory five percent minimum.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the public employees' retirement system to
triage_how: Adds provisions to three Washington public pension systems (TRS, SERS, PERS) allowing members to begin in-service benefit receipt at age 70.5 without leaving employment, without pension reduction.

brief: Providing optional service credit for substitute service to members of the school employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill permits substitute school employees to optionally purchase service credit in the School Employees' Retirement System for substitute service years meeting minimum hour thresholds.

brief: Allowing a member holding state elective office the option during each term of office of membership or retirement and beginning their retirement allowance in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, the teachers' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the public employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: Allows elected state officials who are retirement system members to elect during each term of office to terminate their membership and begin receiving retirement benefits while continuing to serve in elected office.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system plan 1 to use extended school years for calculation of their earnable compensation.
haiku_summary: SB 5096 allows Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members teaching in extended school year programs to calculate earnable compensation using those program years instead of fiscal years, enabling a potentially more favorable basis for retirement benefit computation.

brief: Providing annual increases in retirement allowances.
haiku_summary: The bill extends eligibility for annual postretirement increases in PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 by moving the age determination date from July 1st to December 31st of each calendar year.

brief: Addressing the department of fish and wildlife law enforcement officers' membership in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 for periods of future service.
haiku_summary: Fish and wildlife law enforcement officers who were PERS Plan 2 or Plan 3 members become dual members in LEOFF Plan 2 for future service; PERS Plan 1 members remain in PERS Plan 1.

brief: Creating the select committee on pension policy.
haiku_summary: The bill creates a select committee on pension policy with authority to develop pension funding policies, study the financial condition of state retirement systems, and appoint the state actuary, replacing the prior joint committee structure.

brief: Paying survivor benefits in accordance with Title 26 U.S.C. Sec. 101(h) as amended by the Fallen Hero Survivor Benefit Fairness Act of 2001.
triage_how: Directs that survivor benefits paid under three Washington public retirement systems to beneficiaries of public safety officers who die in the line of duty must comply with federal tax code Section 101(h), allowing tax-free treatment of such benefits.

brief: Correcting retirement system statutes.
haiku_summary: The bill corrects and clarifies retirement system statutes by fixing statutory cross-references, updating beneficiary designation procedures, expanding service transfer eligibility, and removing outdated language.

brief: Creating the license suspension review committee.
triage_how: The bill creates a license suspension review committee to hear appeals from commercial fishers facing suspension or revocation of fishing privileges for violations of fisheries regulations, with no connection to public employee retirement systems.

brief: Increasing the monthly pensions for volunteer fire fighters and reserve officers.
triage_how: Increases monthly pension amounts for volunteer firefighters and reserve officers with 25+ years of service and raises minimum benefit thresholds.

brief: Managing the state's investments.
haiku_summary: The bill restructures the State Investment Board to include beneficiary representatives from major retirement systems and establishes an audit committee with required accountability reporting and outreach to pension participants.

brief:
Limiting the rule-making authority of certain entities to those
instances where there is a specific grant of legislative authority.
haiku_summary: The bill restricts the Department of Retirement Systems director's rule-making authority to require explicit statutory authorization rather than relying on general enabling language.

brief: Retiring early in the public employees' retirement system, plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill replaces the actuarial reduction formula for PERS Plan 2 early retirement benefits with a fixed three percent per year reduction and eliminates the separate alternate early retirement pathway for members with thirty service credit years.

brief: Increasing the duration a liquor license can be summarily suspended.
triage_how: N/A - bill concerns liquor licensing enforcement, not pensions.

brief: Modifying industrial insurance wage provisions.
triage_how: The bill amends industrial insurance (workers compensation) wage calculations and death/disability benefits for work injuries, not public retirement pension systems or benefits.

brief:
Simplifying and adding certainty to the calculation of workers'
compensation benefits.
triage_how: Workers' compensation bill affecting only injury/disability benefit calculations; does not affect public retirement systems.

brief: Making 2003-05 operating appropriations.
haiku_summary: The bill appropriates state contributions to public retirement systems for the 2003-05 fiscal biennium, including $21.2 million annually to LEOFF, $6 million to the judicial retirement system, and $500,000 to the judges retirement system, plus funding for PERS and TRS contributions for judicial and legislative employees.

brief: Implementing tax reform.
haiku_summary: The bill makes pension and retirement benefits from public employees' retirement systems subject to Washington's new state income tax while retaining their exemption from property, sales, and local taxes.

brief: Rehiring retirees of the public employees' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill expands rehiring options for PERS Plan 1 retirees by allowing those separated at least 90 days to work up to 1,500 hours annually in former or current employment while receiving pension, and requires employers to establish formal oversight policies for such rehires subject to state audit.

brief: Making an additional payment to certain plan 1 and plan 3 retirees.
triage_how: The bill authorizes periodic extraordinary investment gain sharing distributions to plan 1 and plan 3 retirees across multiple Washington public retirement systems, with payment amounts calculated using a weighted formula based on service credit and years of retirement.

brief: Participating in insurance plans and contracts by separated plan 2 members of certain retirement systems.
triage_how: Extends health insurance coverage eligibility to Plan 2 members of TRS, SERS, and PERS who are age 55 with at least ten years of service.

brief: Addressing the parks and recreation commission law enforcement officers' membership in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 for periods of future service.
haiku_summary: The bill makes state parks and recreation commission law enforcement officers members of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2, with dual membership for those previously in the public employees' retirement system.

brief: Calculating the death benefits for members of the teachers' retirement system, school employees' retirement system, and public employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill eliminates actuarial reductions to survivor death benefits for members of TRS, SERS, and PERS who are killed in the course of employment, ensuring their beneficiaries receive the full unreduced retirement allowance.

brief: Enhancing industrial insurance vocational rehabilitation benefits.
triage_how: Enhances workers' compensation vocational rehabilitation benefits for injured workers; does not affect public employee pension systems.

brief: Securing hearing loss benefits.
triage_how: Bill modifies workers' compensation procedures for noise-induced hearing loss claims, establishing rate compensation timing and hearing aid appropriateness standards.

brief: Adopting standards under industrial insurance for rating pain-related impairments.
triage_how: Bill amends industrial insurance (workers' compensation) rating standards, not retirement systems.

brief: Concerning industrial insurance medical examinations.
triage_how: Establishes procedures and qualifications for medical examinations ordered in workers' compensation claims, including worker protections, provider standards, and department oversight.

brief: Awarding service credit under the teachers' retirement system plan 1 for military service.
haiku_summary: The bill allows Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members to receive credit for military service performed before joining the system, provided they have completed twenty-five years of service and do not exceed the five-year military service credit limit.

brief: Increasing public employees' retirement system, plan 1 members' monetary compensation for accrued sick leave.
triage_how: Bill enhances sick leave payout for PERS Plan 1 members at retirement to one day's compensation per two days of accrued sick leave (versus one per four days for other employees), with a temporary window for retirements before January 1, 2004.

brief: Establishing a formula for deductions from workers' compensation benefits of inmates and providing for benefits to be sent to department of corrections.
triage_how: Regulates deductions from and redirection of workers' compensation benefits for incarcerated inmates; does not affect public retirement pensions.

brief: Suspending an intermediate driver's license upon a first traffic offense.
triage_how: The bill addresses suspension and revocation of intermediate driver's licenses for traffic offenses by young drivers, with no connection to public retirement systems or benefits.

brief:
Establishing procedures for rehiring retirees of the public employees'
retirement system plan 1 and the teachers' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes procedures allowing PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 retirees to return to employment with a shortened break requirement and without immediate pension suspension, subject to hiring process requirements and annual work hour limits.

brief: Rehiring public employee retirees.
haiku_summary: The bill modifies pension benefit rules for PERS Plan 1 retirees returning to work by raising the hour threshold for those with sufficient break-in-service separation, and requires employers to establish retiree rehiring policies subject to state audit.

brief: Reorganizing criminal statutes within the RCW.
haiku_summary: Bill reorganizes criminal statutes within RCW to simplify citations to criminal offenses but contains no substantive public retirement or pension content.

brief: Extending death benefits to certain surviving spouses under the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill extends survivor death benefits eligibility for the law enforcement and fire fighters' retirement system to allow surviving spouses married fewer than one year at disability to receive benefits if married for at least five years before the member's death and age fifty-five or older.

brief: Changing on a temporary basis the minimum nonforfeiture amounts applicable to certain contracts of life insurance and annuities.
triage_how: Amends insurance regulations governing minimum nonforfeiture amounts in private-sector life insurance and annuity contracts, replacing fixed interest rates with variable rates tied to treasury yields.

brief: Creating a housing allowance program for public school teachers.
haiku_summary: The bill creates a housing allowance program for public school teachers but excludes the allowance from earnable compensation used to calculate pension benefits and contributions.

brief: Providing additional funding for the support of the common schools and state institutions of higher education.
haiku_summary: Subjects retirement and pension benefits to a new two percent state income tax, removing their prior exemption from state taxation.

brief: Changing provisions relating to collection of financial obligations.
triage_how: Bill modifies collection procedures for offenders' financial obligations to allow deduction of workers' compensation benefits for incarcerated inmates with legal financial obligations.

brief: Making an irrevocable choice to waive rights to the defined benefit under the plan 3 retirement systems.
triage_how: The bill allows members of Washington public employee retirement systems (PERS, LEOFF, TRS Plan 3) to irrevocably waive their defined benefit retirement rights after receiving a distribution.

brief: Allowing state and county corrections officers to retire early in the public employees' retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: Creates an early retirement option for corrections officers in PERS Plan 2, allowing retirement at age 55 with 20 years of service credit at a cost of 3 percent annual benefit reduction.

brief: Funding the public employees' retirement system, the teachers' retirement system, and the school employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill updates long-term actuarial assumptions, adjusts employer and member contribution rates for PERS, TRS, SERS, LEOFF, and WSPRS, changes the funding method for plans 2 and 3 from aggregate actuarial cost to projected unit credit with fifteen-year amortization, and reestablishes June 30, 2024 as the full funding target date.

brief: Revising the liability of a spouse for the acts of the other spouse.
triage_how: General marital property law addressing spousal liability for tortious acts and unauthorized debt; makes no distinction for retirement benefits or systems.

brief: Relating to retirement from public service.
triage_how: The bill XML contains only a title section and no substantive legislative provisions addressing public retirement systems or benefits.

brief: Relating to retirement from public service.
triage_how: The bill contains no substantive provisions—only a single section naming the act, with no amendments to pension RCWs or changes to retirement benefits.

brief: Providing public employment retirement credits and education fee waivers for veterans of the Afghanistan conflict and the Persian Gulf War I
triage_how: Expands the definition of veteran in public employment pension law (RCW 41.04.005) to include Afghanistan conflict and Persian Gulf War II veterans, extending access to existing veteran benefits in the state retirement systems.

brief: Concerning treatment of injured workers covered by industrial insurance.
triage_how: Bill amends RCW Title 51 provisions governing workers' compensation treatment protocols and medical care for work-injured workers; does not affect public employee retirement pension systems.

brief: Implementing tax reform.
haiku_summary: Bill removes exemption from state income tax for public pension and retirement benefits by subjecting them to the new income tax established under Title 82A.

brief: Establishing a public safety employees' retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes the Washington Public Safety Employees' Retirement System Plan 2, a new retirement plan for state and local public safety employees, and permits eligible Public Employees' Retirement System members to elect transfer to the new system during a specified election period.

brief: Vesting after five years of service in the defined benefit portion of the public employees' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the teachers' retirement system plan 3.
haiku_summary: The bill reduces the vesting requirement for normal retirement eligibility from ten years to five years of service credit in PERS, SERS, and TRS Plan 3.

brief: Providing annual increases in retirement allowances.
haiku_summary: The bill extends the age eligibility deadline for annual postretirement increases in PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 from July 1 to December 31 of the benefit year, allowing retirees to reach age 66 later in the calendar year to qualify for that year's increase.

brief: Establishing an asset smoothing corridor for actuarial valuations used in the funding of the state retirement systems.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes an asset smoothing corridor (70-130 percent of market value) for the actuarial value of assets used in calculating state retirement system funding contributions, with investment return deviations from long-term assumptions recognized over periods up to eight years.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system plan 1 who are employed less than full time as psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, or speech language pathologists or audiologists to annualize their salaries when calculating their average final compensation.
haiku_summary: The bill allows part-time Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members employed as psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, or speech language pathologists or audiologists to annualize their salaries when calculating average final compensation for retirement benefits.

brief: Permitting members of the public employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3, the school employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3,
triage_how: The bill permits qualifying members of three Washington public retirement systems to purchase additional service credit upon retirement, increasing their pension benefits.

brief: Permitting members of the public employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 and the school employees' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 to buy down the early retirement reduction amounts.
haiku_summary: Bill permits members of PERS and SERS Plans 2 and 3 to purchase a reduction in the early retirement benefit penalty through lump sum payments, rollovers, or transfers from eligible retirement plans.

brief: Establishing a one thousand dollar minimum monthly benefit for public employees' retirement system plan 1 members and teachers' retirement system plan 1 members who have at least twenty five years of service and who have been retired at least twenty years.
haiku_summary: The bill establishes a $1,000 monthly minimum benefit for PERS Plan 1 and TRS Plan 1 members with at least 25 years of service who have been retired at least 20 years, effective July 1, 2004.

brief: Providing death benefits for members of the Washington state patrol retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill exempts survivor retirement allowances from actuarial reduction when a Washington State Patrol member is killed in the course of employment.

brief: Calculating the retirement allowance of a member of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 who is killed in the course of employment.
haiku_summary: The bill removes the actuarial reduction on retirement allowances for beneficiaries of LEOFF Plan 2 members killed in the course of employment, allowing them to receive the full computed allowance.

brief: Providing benefits to certain disabled members of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill enhances disability retirement benefits for LEOFF Plan 2 members disabled in the line of duty by establishing a minimum monthly disability allowance of 10 percent of final average salary plus 2 percent per year of service beyond five years, and allowing such members who leave employment to request a refund of 150 percent of accumulated contributions.

brief: Expanding the role of self-insurers in the workers' compensation system.
triage_how: Bill expands self-insurer authority in workers' compensation claims administration within RCW 51.x.x; contains no provisions affecting pension systems, pension eligibility, or pension benefits.

brief: Establishing the composition and jurisdiction of city and county disability boards.
haiku_summary: The bill clarifies the composition and jurisdiction of city and county disability boards that adjudicate disability claims for fire fighters and law enforcement officers, refining employment-based eligibility and board position substitution rules.

brief: Regulating postretirement public employment.
haiku_summary: The bill reduces the annual hours threshold at which postretirement retirees must suspend pension benefits to 867 hours, while creating exceptions for positions with documented justifiable need.

brief: Authorizing collection of support payments for children with developmental disabilities in out-of-home care.
triage_how: Bill is exclusively about child support collection and child welfare; it does not affect retirement benefits or pension systems.

brief: Changing provisions relating to industrial insurance claims.
triage_how: Bill amends industrial insurance claims processing and administration; does not affect public retirement benefits or systems.

brief: Concerning applications for compensation under the industrial insurance system.
triage_how: Modifies workers' compensation claims procedures and reporting timelines under RCW 51, with no effect on public retirement systems or pension benefits.

brief: Providing remuneration for unused sick leave for public employees retirement system plan 3 members.
triage_how: Allows PERS Plan 3 members age 55 and older with 10 or more years of service credit to receive unused sick leave compensation at service separation rather than retirement, though such remuneration is excluded from retirement benefit calculations.

brief: Awarding service credit under the teachers' retirement system plan 1 for military service.
haiku_summary: Bill allows Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members with 25 years of creditable service to receive credit for military service performed before system membership, subject to contribution requirements and a five-year aggregate limit on military service credit.

brief: Requiring senate confirmation of certain commission and department appointments.
haiku_summary: The bill requires senate confirmation for representatives of public retirement systems appointed to the State Investment Board.

brief: Establishing requirement for reporting reprimands and stayed suspensions against certificated staff.
triage_how: Bill establishes reporting requirements for disciplinary actions against certificated staff but contains no pension provisions.

brief: Transferring service credit into the Washington school employees' retirement system, plan 2.
haiku_summary: The bill modifies the process for Plan 2 members of the Washington School Employees' Retirement System to optionally restore previously withdrawn service credit and contributions, replacing an automatic membership transfer requirement for inactive members with a voluntary restoration option.

brief: Conforming the social security offset provisions of Title 51 RCW to the modified federal social security retirement age and continuing to allow the state to implement an offset otherwise imposed by the federal government.
triage_how: Bill amends Title 51 RCW workers' compensation disability offset provisions to conform to modified federal Social Security retirement age, affecting only workers' compensation benefits.

brief: Concerning liability to the department of labor and industries for premiums, overpayments, and penalties.
triage_how: Amends workers' compensation premium liability, contractor obligations, fraud definitions, and overpayment collection procedures in Title 51 RCW.

brief: Awarding service credit under the teachers' retirement system plan 1 for military service.
haiku_summary: The bill permits Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members to purchase credit for military service performed prior to system membership, provided they have completed 25 years of creditable service, with total military credit capped at five years and requiring contributions of six percent of average earnable compensation.

brief: Authorizing retired local government employees to receive benefits from the public employees' benefits board.
triage_how: Bill extends health insurance coverage through the public employees' benefits board to retired local government employees who are members of the Public Employees' Retirement System.

brief: Making 2005-07 operating appropriations based on current law.
haiku_summary: The bill adds the Teachers' Retirement System (Chapter 41.37) to the Department of Retirement Systems' administrative expense allocation and billing structure.

brief: Making 2005-07 operating appropriations.
haiku_summary: The bill appropriates funding for Department of Retirement Systems operations and state contributions to retirement systems for the 2005-07 biennium and amends RCW 41.50.110 to revise how retirement system administration expenses are allocated to employers.

brief: Adjusting public pension gain-sharing increase amounts.
haiku_summary: The bill ends automatic gain-sharing pension increases and requires future increases to be authorized by the legislature.

brief: Changing pension funding methodology.
haiku_summary: The bill updates pension funding methodology by adjusting economic assumptions in actuarial valuations and implements phased annual contribution rate increases from 2005 to 2009, with suspension of unfunded liability payments for Plan 1 systems during 2005-2007.

brief: Reorganizing public disclosure law.
haiku_summary: The bill reorganizes Washington public disclosure law by creating a new public records act chapter and recodifying related statutes.

brief: Providing administrative review before the suspension of driving privileges.
triage_how: This bill concerns only administrative procedures for suspending driving privileges for traffic violations and has no substantive connection to Washington public retirement systems, plans, or benefits.

brief: Permitting members of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2 to make a one-time purchase of add
triage_how: It allows LEOFF Plan 2 members to purchase up to five years of additional service credit at retirement, directly increasing their pension benefit under the statutory framework of chapter 41.26 RCW.

brief: Suspending a retirement allowance upon reemployment.
haiku_summary: The bill allows LEOFF Plan 2 retirees upon reemployment to elect to enter a new retirement system or continue receiving retirement benefits without suspension.

brief: Receiving a disability allowance under the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, plan 2.
haiku_summary: House Bill 1271 establishes a seventy percent final average salary disability benefit for law enforcement and fire fighters totally disabled in the line of duty under LEOFF Plan 2, without actuarial reduction to age fifty-three.

brief: Authorizing the health care authority to receive a federal employer subsidy for continuing to provide a pharmacy benefit to retirees.
triage_how: This bill does not substantively concern WA public retirement systems or their benefits; it addresses health insurance coverage and pharmacy subsidies for retired public employees, which is a separate benefit program administered through the Public Employees' Benefits Board.

brief: Changing member contribution rates in the Washington state patrol retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill reduces member contribution rates in the Washington state patrol retirement system by establishing the rate as the lesser of seven percent or one-third of the employer rate, with a floor of two percent.

brief: Allowing certain members of the teachers', school employees', and public employees' retirement systems to return to work without restrictions or begin receiving their retirement allowance before separation from state elective office.
haiku_summary: The bill allows members of TRS, SERS, and PERS who retire at or after age 70.5 to return to work and continue receiving pension payments without restrictions, except that state elected officials are excluded unless they leave office or are subsequently reappointed or reelected.

brief: Survivor benefits for ex spouses in the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill expands survivor benefits for ex-spouses of LEOFF Plan 1 members by replacing restrictive eligibility criteria with a simpler standard based on court decree provisions.

brief: Changing the terms for vesting after five years of service in the defined benefit portion of the public employees' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, and the teachers' retirement system plan 3.
haiku_summary: The bill lowers the age requirement for five-year vesting eligibility from age 54 to age 44 in the defined benefit portions of PERS, SERS, and TRS Plan 3.

brief: Allowing members of the teachers' retirement system plan 1 who are employed less than full time as psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, or speech language pathologists or audiologists to annualize their salaries when calculating their average final compensation.
haiku_summary: Allows part-time TRS Plan 1 members who are psychologists, social workers, nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, or speech language pathologists/audiologists to annualize their salaries when calculating average final compensation for retirement benefits.

brief: Purchasing service credit in plan 2 and plan 3 of the teachers' retirement system for public education experience performed as a teache
triage_how: The bill amends RCW 41.32 to allow TRS members to purchase prior service credit for out-of-state teaching experience, directly altering TRS benefit accrual.

brief: Changing the membership of the executive committee of the select committee on pension policy.
haiku_summary: The bill expands the Select Committee on Pension Policy's executive committee from five to six members and adds a retiree representative from state retirement systems while removing the office of financial management director.

brief: Replacing gain-sharing provisions with certain changes in benefits and setting contribution rates for the public employees', teachers', school employees', and public safety employees' retirement systems.
haiku_summary: The bill replaces the extraordinary investment gain-sharing distribution with a simplified fixed benefit formula and standardizes employee contribution rates to employer combined plan rates for public employee retirement systems.

brief: Authorizing interruptive military service credit.
haiku_summary: The bill allows surviving spouses and eligible children of members who died while serving in the uniformed services to claim military service credit on behalf of the deceased member.

brief: Restricting the public employment of retirees from the teachers' retirement system and the public employees' retirement system.
haiku_summary: The bill restricts public employment of retirees from TRS and PERS by suspending pension benefits when retirees work over 867 hours annually, effectively limiting retirees to approximately five months of employment per year while receiving full pension payments.

brief: Permitting members of the teachers' retirement system plan 2 and plan 3 who qualify for early retirement or alternate early retirement
triage_how: The bill substantively amends the Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) by adding new sections to RCW 41.32, permitting TRS Plan 2 and Plan 3 members to purchase up to five years of additional service credit at retirement, directly affecting public retirement benefits.

brief: Establishing the composition and jurisdiction of city and county disability boards.
haiku_summary: The bill clarifies the jurisdictional basis and composition of city and county disability boards by establishing they have authority over members employed by or retired from employers within their territories and allowing flexible representation when counties lack fire fighters or law enforcement officers.

brief: Choosing a reduced retirement allowance under the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system, plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill modifies LEOFF Plan 1 to expand eligibility for members to reduce their retirement allowance in exchange for post-death survivor benefits payable to an otherwise-ineligible spouse.

brief: Making technical corrections in the general retirement provisions estoppel section, teachers' retirement system, public safety employees' retirement system, the school employees' retirement system, the public employees' retirement system, and the actuarial funding chapter.
haiku_summary: The bill clarifies cross-system employment restrictions for pension retirees and consolidates redundant administrative requirements across the state retirement systems.

brief: Revising provisions relating to contract liquor stores.
haiku_summary: Bill updates liquor control terminology, changing references from "agency vendors" to "contract liquor store managers" but makes no substantive changes to retirement system rules.

brief: Participating in insurance plans and contracts by separated plan 2 members of certain retirement systems.
triage_how: The bill extends health insurance eligibility to separated employees from Plan 2 retirement systems but does not substantively concern pension benefits, plan design, or eligibility rules; it uses retirement system membership only as a qualifying criterion for a separate health insurance benefit.

brief: Crediting military service to certain employees.
haiku_summary: The bill liberalizes military service credit eligibility for public employees by eliminating the 90-day reemployment deadline, extending timelines to one year, and allowing members with 25 years of service to claim military service credit regardless of employment status.

brief: Identifying health care providers covered by the retired health care provider liability malpractice insurance program.
triage_how: The bill establishes insurance coverage for volunteer retired healthcare providers at low-income clinics, not a public employee retirement system or pension benefit program.

brief: Raising the mandatory retirement age for members of the Washington state patrol retirement system.
haiku_summary: Raises the mandatory retirement age for Washington State Patrol members from age 60 to age 61.

brief: Creating the Washington voluntary accounts program.
haiku_summary: Establishes a voluntary retirement savings account program for private-sector employees without access to employer-based retirement plans.

brief: Allowing terminally ill members to remove themselves from their retirement plan.
haiku_summary: The bill allows members diagnosed with a terminal illness with life expectancy of five or fewer years to withdraw from retirement system membership upon medical certification and director concurrence, ceasing contributions and service credit accrual.

brief: Restructuring certain transportation agencies.
haiku_summary: This bill does not substantively change public retirement or pensions; it only removes administrative references to transportation committees being restructured.

brief: Changing provisions relating to the administrative office of the courts.
haiku_summary: The bill updates the Judges' Retirement Account provisions to reference the "administrative office of the courts" rather than the "administrator for the courts" in handling member accumulated contributions and beneficiary designations.

brief: Reducing the regulatory burden for Washington businesses.
haiku_summary: Restricts the Department of Retirement Systems director's authority to adopt administrative rules to those derived from specific legislative grants of authority.

brief: Simplifying and adding certainty to the calculation of workers' compensation benefits.
triage_how: The bill modifies workers' compensation benefit calculations under RCW 51 (industrial injury insurance), which is unrelated to public employee retirement systems.

brief: Allowing additional industrial insurance benefits when social security benefits are reduced.
triage_how: It allows workers to request adjustments to industrial insurance disability benefits when federal Social Security disability benefits are retroactively reduced, addressing a coordination issue in workers' compensation law rather than pension law.

brief: Creating a task force on public recreational lands and public safety.
haiku_summary: This bill does not concern public retirement or pensions; it creates a task force to review law enforcement authority and coordination at state parks and natural resource lands.

brief: Awarding service credit under the teachers' retirement system plan 1 for military service.
haiku_summary: The bill allows Teachers' Retirement System Plan 1 members to receive service credit for military service performed before joining the system, provided they have completed at least 25 years of creditable service and make required member contributions.

brief: Creating a retired volunteer medical worker license.
triage_how: The bill creates a special occupational license category for formerly licensed healthcare professionals to volunteer in emergency services, using "retired" to denote licensing status rather than addressing any public employee pension system, retirement benefit, or contribution provision.

brief: Expanding the role of self-insurers in the workers' compensation system.
triage_how: The bill expands self-insurer authority in workers' compensation claims under RCW 51; references to "pension" concern permanent disability benefits within the workers' compensation system, not public retirement systems.

brief: Making costofliving adjustments to account for inflation in industrial insurance claims.
triage_how: It adjusts death and disability benefit maximums under Washington's industrial insurance (workers' compensation) system for inflation, which is separate from public retirement pension systems.

brief: Removing the cap on retirement benefits of members of the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 1.
haiku_summary: The bill removes the 60 percent cap on retirement allowances for members of the Law Enforcement Officers' and Fire Fighters' Retirement System Plan 1.

brief: Modifying the definition of wages.
triage_how: It modifies workers compensation wage calculations under industrial insurance law, which is a separate benefit system from public retirement pensions and does not affect pension benefit determinations.

brief: Using wage assignment orders to enforce health insurance coverage.
triage_how: The bill does not substantively affect public retirement systems or benefits; it addresses child support health insurance enforcement through wage assignment procedures.

brief: Allowing members of the public employees' retirement system plans 1 and 2 employed as emergency medical technicians to transfer to the law enforcement officers' and fire fighters' retirement system plan 2.
